sentences.text: Revenue, net interest income plus noninterest income, rose from $96.6 billion in FY2016 to $182 billion in FY2025, a 7.3% CAGR [D5][D206].
The path was a step change rather than smooth compounding: revenue grew 22.9% in FY2023 and 12.3% in FY2024, against 1.4% in FY2021 [D179][D202][D129].
The FY2023 step came from higher rates lifting net interest income, which rose 33.8% that year [D174], with deposit margin expansion on higher rates cited in the filings [P37].
Net income compounded at 9.7% over the window [F113], and the FY2025 revenue gain slowed to 2.8% [D226].
North America supplied the bulk of growth, contributing 20.6pp of the FY2023 revenue increase and 10.2pp in FY2024, at 76.6% of FY2025 revenue [D245][D248][D249].
In FY2025 the largest contributions were EMEA at +1.2pp and Asia-Pacific at +1.2pp, while North America added only +0.2pp [D276][D301][D251].
FY2025 net interest income rose 3.1% [D221], driven by higher Markets net interest income and higher revolving balances in Card Services, largely offset by deposit margin compression [P28].
Operating costs grew 4.2% against revenue growth of 2.8%, so operating costs grew 1.4pp faster than revenue [D225][D226].
Diluted EPS grew 13.9% a year against 9.7% for net income [F115][F113], helped by a 3.4% share-count reduction in FY2025 [D224].
The efficiency ratio was 52.4% in FY2025, below the 57.2% window median and above the 51.7% window low [D207][D333][D331].
The credit-loss provision was 7.8% of revenue in FY2025, up from 6.0% in FY2024 and above the 6.0% peer median [D208][D185][D341].
The FY2025 provision rose on net increases in the loan and lending-related commitment portfolios and an update to loss assumptions on certain leveraged loans [P15].
Net margin of 31.2% sat 21.2pp below the 52.4% efficiency ratio's complement, reflecting the 21.4% effective tax rate and the provision [D210][D207][D203].
Operating cash flow is not a meaningful earnings-quality measure for a bank; it was -$148 billion in FY2025 against net income of $57.0 billion [F60][F30].
The FY2025 outflow resulted from higher trading assets, higher securities borrowed, and net originations and purchases of loans held-for-sale [P21].
Capital return, buybacks plus dividends, was $48.2 billion in FY2025 against net income of $57.0 billion [D205][F30].
Return on average equity was 16.1% in FY2025, in the 100th percentile of the seven-bank peer group against an 11.8% median [D213][D338][D339].
The efficiency ratio sat in the 0th percentile against a 61.7% peer median [D336][D337].
Loans were 57.3% of deposits in FY2025, up from 43.1% in FY2021 [D211][D115].
Loans rose $121 billion, driven by higher CIB loans, primarily in Markets, and higher securities-based lending in AWM [P4].
Buybacks of $31.6 billion and dividends of $16.6 billion were funded alongside a 3.4% reduction in diluted shares [X102][X112][D224].
Net income for FY2021 through FY2025 in the metrics table comes from the proxy statement's pay-versus-performance table, not the 10-K, differing by up to 0.10% [R1][F26][X16][F30][X20].
The gap is immaterial to ratios but matters where precision is claimed, so the 10-K figures should be cited [R1].
FY2020 pretax income and income tax were later restated, and the pack uses the first-reported values [R2][R3][X63][X73].
This affects only FY2020 comparisons and does not change the trend described [R2][R3].
Whether the efficiency ratio holds below the 57.2% window median or rises toward the 59.2% window high, reported in the FY2026 10-K [D333][D332].
Whether the credit-loss provision as a share of revenue stays above the 6.0% peer median or falls back toward the 5.9% FY2023 level [D341][D161].
Whether net interest income growth stays above the 3.1% FY2025 rate or turns negative as in FY2021's -4.1% [D221][D124].
